channel.title: Lumeshot
channel.description: Updates for Lumeshot, a screenshot and screen-recording tool for macOS.

item.description:
One change, to how the annotation editor's window is sized.
## The editor opens larger and remembers your size
The editor window opened small enough that marking up a capture felt cramped, and if you resized it the size was forgotten by the next capture.
It now opens at a generous default — up to 1200×780, capped to fit your screen and never smaller than 760×480 — and it **remembers the size and position you set**, so a one-time resize sticks for the next capture and the next launch. The window has always been resizable; this just gives it a roomier starting size and makes your own size stick.

One change, refining the look of the annotation editor's tool list.
## The editing tools now read as a native sidebar
The tool rail on the left of the editor has been reworked to look and feel like a standard macOS sidebar. The tools are organised under quiet section headers — **Shapes** (Select, Rectangle, Ellipse, Line, Arrow, Freehand), **Redact** (Blur, Pixelate) and **Annotate** (Text, Highlighter, Step, Crop) — the sidebar carries the system's translucent material, and the active tool is shown as a full, accent-coloured row the way selection looks in Finder and Mail.
Nothing about what the tools do has changed; the list is just easier to scan and more at home on macOS.

One change, to make the annotation editor's tools easier to recognise.
## The editing tools are now a labelled rail
The editor's drawing tools used to be a row of icon-only buttons along the top, sharing space with the colour, width and finish controls — you had to hover each one to find out what it did.
They now sit in a vertical rail down the left side of the editor, each shown as an icon **and** its name — Select, Rectangle, Ellipse, Line, Arrow, Freehand, Crop, Text, Highlighter, Blur, Pixelate, Step — with the active tool highlighted. The top bar keeps the colour, stroke width, undo/redo/delete and the Cancel / Copy / Save / Upload buttons. Nothing about what the tools do has changed; they are just easier to tell apart. With the tools moved out of the top row, the editor window also opens at a more compact size again.
